question.worked_solution:
To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, we consider the expressions inside each of the parentheses. The first one is.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}\times {(-5)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying PEMDAS to this expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}\times {(-5)}^{2} & = \\ \frac{2}{5}\times 25 & = \\ \frac{2}{5}\times \frac{25}{1} & = \\ \frac{2\times 25}{5\times 1} & = \\ \frac{50}{5} & = \\ 10\end{aligned}
$$

The expression inside the second parentheses is.

$$
\begin{aligned}{(-2)}^{5}-(-20).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying PEMDAS to this expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(-2)}^{5}-(-20) & = \\ (-32)+20 & = \\ -12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{2}{5}\times {(-5)}^{2})÷({(-2)}^{5}-(-20)) & = \\ 10÷(-12) & = \\ \frac{10}{(-12)} & = \\ -\frac{10}{12} & = \\ -\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
